title: The long history
tomorrow: why did the man at the masjid pray with his arms at his sides?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the companions: the perfume seller and the bellows, and the people who walked close enough to carry him home. Good company. Today, everyone who carried it after them.

Some heirlooms come with a list. Inside the cover of an old Qur'an in a Houston living room, there are names in different handwriting: a great-grandfather's in faded brown ink, a grandfather's in pencil, then Dadi Fatima's in blue ballpoint. Under hers, an empty line. She slides the book across the table to her granddaughter and doesn't say a word. It's what happens when someone hands you a watch, a recipe, a family name. Suddenly you're standing in a line, and it's longer than you thought.
screen: `NAMES INSIDE THE COVER.` → `AN EMPTY LINE.` → `LONGER THAN YOU THOUGHT.`

segments.voice: Every hadith on this path arrived with a list of names too. So-and-so told me that so-and-so told him that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say. That chain is the isnad, and the scholars who gathered hadith weighed every link: who was honest, whose memory was sound, who had actually met whom. One to tell a friend tonight: in the introduction to Sahih Muslim, the scholar Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak is quoted saying the isnad is part of the religion, and without it anyone could say whatever they liked. A faith carried by named people, hand to hand. And the Qur'an turns that line into a prayer. Describing the believers who came later, it gives their words: "Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith." Not only their own parents. Everyone ahead of them in the line, known or unknown. That's the long history from the inside. Not dates in a textbook, but a relay: a grandmother teaching the Fatiha at a kitchen table, a teacher at a mosque whose name nobody wrote down, a traveler who carried one hadith to a new city. Each held it for a while and handed it on. When you pray for them, the line runs backward too. You're not at the end of it. You're the newest name, with a space under yours.
screen: `THE ISNAD: A CHAIN OF NAMES.` · `PART OF THE RELIGION.` · `FORGIVE THOSE BEFORE US.` · `A RELAY, NOT A TEXTBOOK.` · then, large: `THE LONG LINE.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and walk back along your own line: someone who taught you a prayer or a kindness, the person who taught them, and further back, people whose names you'll never know. If you pray, you can use the Qur'an's words for them: "Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith." If not, hold them in mind one at a time until the time is up.
screen: `WALK BACK ALONG YOUR LINE.` · `NAMES YOU KNOW, NAMES YOU DON'T.` · `HOLD THEM, ONE AT A TIME.`

segments.voice: The long history: believers carrying the faith hand to hand, named in chains, remembered in prayer.
Your line: the long line, and the space waiting under your name. Seven of fifteen, past halfway.

screen: `DAY 1783 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 7 OF 15.` → `TOMORROW: WHY DID HE PRAY WITH HIS ARMS AT HIS SIDES?`

howItsDone: Hadith are taught with their chains of narrators, the isnad, and Muslims pray for those who came before them in faith, often using the words of Qur'an 59:10; many families pass down a Qur'an through the generations.
